findings.title: Unsubscribe action crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (any logged-in user who never visited/interacted with that visible topic — e.g. a colleague who opens a forwarded unsubscribe link, or a user hitting the URL manually). The very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, and later `tu.save!`, so a nil result produces an unhandled NoMethodError (HTTP 500) on a user-facing endpoint. The action should use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or guard against nil.

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change and leaves notifications_reason_id nil
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates the notification level with `tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change` (which `set_notifications` uses). `TopicUser.change` sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id = :user_changed`, and publishes the change on MessageBus. Writing directly leaves `notifications_reason_id` as nil. Both `TopicUser.update_last_read` (its `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null ... then :tracking`) and `TopicUser.auto_track` (guarded on `notifications_reason_id: nil`) will re-upgrade a topic to tracking/watch based on continued reading whenever the reason is nil. So the user unsubscribes, then normal reading silently re-subscribes them — the feature does not stick. It also skips the MessageBus publish, so an open client won't reflect the new level.

findings.title: State-changing action performed via GET allows CSRF
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is routed as `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` (and the no-slug variant) and mutates the user's notification level. Rails CSRF protection only covers non-GET requests, and this action additionally does `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. A logged-in user who loads any third-party page containing `` will be silently unsubscribed from that topic. The action should require a non-idempotent method (POST/DELETE) with CSRF, or use a signed token so mere navigation cannot trigger the change.

findings.title: New unsubscribe_url option and unsubscribe endpoint have no meaningful tests
findings.body: The spec adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to `message_with_unsubscribe`, but only so the new `unsubscribe_link` locale interpolation doesn't raise; nothing asserts that the per-topic URL actually appears in the generated email body or that it is formatted correctly (the real value is an absolute URL while the spec passes a relative one). There is also no spec at all for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (nil TopicUser, watching→regular vs regular→muted transitions, slug redirect). The core behavior of this PR is effectively untested, so a regression would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Email unsubscribe text overstates behavior for tracking/watching topics
findings.body: For a topic at tracking or watching level the action downgrades to `regular` (`if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ... = :regular`), not mute. But the email/client text claims `stop_notifications: "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."` A user who was watching still receives notifications on replies and mentions, so the message is misleading and they will be surprised to keep getting email for a topic they clicked to unsubscribe from.
